spec_issues: The overview says the agent 'may tune these choices on 864 public labeled examples but not memorize any example's label'. The prompt says 'do not store example-specific answers'. Neither defines whether few-shot demos copied from public rows are allowed (Gemini Flash MrsL85q, Grok cxmH3Ca, and Argon 8xeEGY4's prompt examples), or rule cascades fitted to zero public error. The undisclosed disqualification process did not act on any of them.

The task is framed as improving the Qwen3-4B self-judge, but nothing requires the model to be called. Both Grok final judges used 0 prompt and 0 generation tokens on the public run, as pure regex/lexical classifiers. That is outside the stated research question, yet scored.

The 3% BER floor (MIN_BER = 0.03, 'Chosen scoring floor') is below what most strong judges reach on the public set (0.015-0.026). Public reward saturates at about 6.1-6.18, so agents get no signal to choose among top candidates. Kimi dmKYJuz [1340]: 'reward mathematically frozen'. No trial hit the floor on the private set (best 0.0346).
verifier_issues: Objective: BER = 0.5*(false-accept rate + false-reject rate) on 1,948 private rows from two sources (public: dqa1 518 rows, multihop 346; 648 correct and 216 wrong). Reward = baseline_BER / max(BER, 0.03) - 1, with lower BER better. Because BER is balanced, rejecting everything scores 0.5 and accepting everything 0.5; neither class prior nor 'reject almost everything' helps. The reference answer is a legitimate judge input, so 'using the answer key' is the task itself. There is no label leakage: the judge sees only question, reference and answer, and the labels come from two page-reading models.
The baseline BER is re-measured per trial (0.2070, 0.2081, 0.2091), a ~1% denominator noise. This is negligible next to the gaps between models.

Every trial degrades from public to private: clean model-based judges by about 2-3x (Fable 0.017->0.035; GPT iR2q9m5 0.017->0.043; Kimi dmKYJuz 0.015->0.050), and the rule-heavy ones far more (Argon 8xeEGY4 0.000->0.055; Grok cxmH3Ca 0.000->0.094; Grok VWjtLSg 0.000->0.169). The private set correctly penalises public overfitting, so official rewards reflect generalisation. The exception is the rule breach in Grok cxmH3Ca, which the grader did not disqualify.
task_level.noise: With about 490 wrong rows (assuming the public 25% ratio), the private BER standard error is about 0.005. Because reward is 0.209/BER - 1, small BER gaps near the floor become large reward gaps: Fable 0.0346 vs GPT 0.0428 is 1.2 reward points but only about 1.5 SE. BER order: Fable 0.035/0.035 < GPT 0.043/0.048 < Kimi 0.050/0.056 ~ Argon 0.055/0.065 < Grok cxmH3Ca 0.094 < Flash 0.106/0.130 < Grok VWjtLSg 0.169. Fable's two attempts are both best, so the winner is plausible. The Kimi/Argon/GPT boundary is within noise.
task_level.epoch_rationale: One false positive (Grok cxmH3Ca, memorised public rows, scored 1.23) changes Grok's pairwise results against both Flash trials and its own other attempt. It does not change the winner (Fable, with the best BER on both attempts), and the metric itself is balanced and measured on unseen rows.
task_level.science_vs_gaming: Most of the 2-6x reward is real and comes from simple, transferable judge-design findings. Reading P(YES) log-probs with a tuned threshold removes the starter's sycophantic ~40% false-accept rate; Flash cWScLtn gets BER 0.13 from that alone. Strict 'every reference fact must be present' wording, answer-before-reference ordering (Fable), multi-prompt logit ensembles, reference decomposition into checked claims (Kimi, GPT), logistic calibration, and spending the averaged token budget only on ambiguous rows bring BER to about 0.035-0.05. These are known LLM-as-judge techniques, applied well. Gaming appears in Grok cxmH3Ca (hundreds of rules keyed to public rows). Over-fitting to the public set appears in Grok VWjtLSg and Argon 8xeEGY4 (public BER 0), and Flash MrsL85q stores public rows as few-shots. Only Grok cxmH3Ca clearly breaks the stated rule.

trials.approach: Stage 1 runs three single-token YES/NO 'coverage' prompts ('does the candidate state every piece of information in the reference?'), with the candidate answer shown BEFORE the reference, and averages their first-token log-odds. Rows inside a calibrated uncertainty band get a short thinking-mode call through the completions endpoint; truncated thinking gets a forced verdict under a stricter threshold. Global token banks pool the per-row budget across rows. Public BER 0.019 (floored to 0.03); private 0.0352.

trials.approach: A 6-prompt first-token YES/NO log-prob ensemble with mean-logit fusion and a global acceptance threshold of 4.1. Rows in a borderline band get a 'claim-coverage rescue': the reference is decomposed into atomic key points, each point is checked against the answer, and the row is rescued if all are covered (max over 3 decompositions). Public BER 0.026; private 0.0558.

trials.approach: The model decomposes the reference into a checklist. Items are kept only if grounded in the reference text. Each item gets a one-word coverage probe, scored by first-token log-probs, at two granularities.
